title: Mirabel and the Atlas
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, on the eve of revolution, Felix Thackeray works her late father's type-cutting bench in a print shop that quietly produces seditious pamphlets alongside almanacs. When an unknown woman leaves a feverish child at the shop door with a carved atlas plate hidden in his swaddling and one instruction — forget my face — Felix discovers the plate is a map of the regime's coastal fortifications, cut in her father's own hand before his death. To honor both her father's memory and the found family of printers who raised her, she must carry the plate past three military checkpoints to a smuggler's ship sailing on the morning tide, pursued by the inspector who once loved her mother. She delivers the map at terrible cost — the shop burns, her mentor is taken — but the evidence reaches the revolutionary fleet, and years later Felix cuts the first typeface of the free press with the child, now hers, at her side.
about_author: W. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in harbor towns from Lisbon to Marseille. Their novels examine what working hands remember that official histories do not.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On the last ordinary day, Felix measures the print shop's inventory — type, paper, her father's unfinished dies — against rumors that the army will seize the presses. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; she inherits her father's habit of counting what can be carried.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. During a blackout curfew, a woman leaves a sick toddler and a wrapped copper plate, whispering 'forget my face' before vanishing into the fog. The shop's master printer, Odile, recognizes the plate's cutting style and goes pale. Emotional beat: fear braided with fierce, immediate protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Plate Shows
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. By candlelight, the printers study the atlas plate: fortifications, gun emplacements, escape routes — engraved in Thackeray's unmistakable hand, dated after his supposed death. Emotional beat: grief reopened; the dead father becomes a conspirator, and Felix's inheritance turns dangerous.

chapters.title: Inspector Corvain Calls
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The regime's inspector searches the shop under pretext of a licensing audit, lingering over Felix's father's old bench. She hides the child in the type cabinet and lies for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve; the enemy has a familiar face.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The network plans the route: the fish market gate, the customs house, the quay patrol — each checkpoint deadlier than the last. Odile argues she should carry the plate; Felix refuses, claiming the right as the cutter's daughter. Emotional beat: found family fracturing over who gets to be brave.

chapters.title: The Fish Market Gate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with the plate sewn into a fishmonger's basket. A soldier she grew up with waves her through — then is ordered to search every basket as she passes the far side. Emotional beat: luck and guilt in equal measure; the first checkpoint passed by grace, not skill.

chapters.title: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Caught in a document check, Felix bluffs her way through by typesetting a forged pass on the spot — her father's craft saving her. But Corvain arrives, recognizing her hand's resemblance to Thackeray's. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into exposure; she escapes only because a riot erupts outside.

chapters.title: Fire at the Sign of the Atlas
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Soldiers torch the print shop while Felix is on the quay; Odile stays behind to destroy the archives and is arrested. Watching her home burn across the water, Felix clutches the plate and the child. Emotional beat: devastation transmuted into certainty — there is no going back.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the final checkpoint on the quay, Corvain corners her — and lets her pass, revealing he loved her mother and owes Thackeray a debt he never repaid. Felix boards the smuggler's ship as dawn breaks and hands the atlas plate to the fleet's agent. Emotional beat: mercy from an unexpected quarter; the climax resolved not by force but by a man choosing memory over duty.

chapters.title: First Letters
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, five years later. In a liberated Vellamare, Felix cuts the opening typeface for the new republic's press, the rescued child — now calling her Mama — sorting sorts beside her. Odile returns from prison, thinner but laughing. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; memory kept not by forgetting a face, but by building something worth remembering.
